questions.question: The emergency provisions of the Indian Constitution are borrowed from the Government of India Act, ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1935**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The emergency provisions of the Indian Constitution are borrowed from the Government of India Act, **1935**.
 
• The Government of India Act 1935 was a comprehensive statute that laid the foundation for the federal structure and significant administrative reforms in British India.
 
• Provisions under this act included the establishment of a Federal Court, the division of powers between the centre and provinces, and emergency powers.
 
• The Indian Constitution adopted many features from this act, including the emergency provisions allowing the President to declare an emergency in case of war, external aggression, or armed rebellion.
 
• These emergency provisions ensure that the central government can take swift and decisive action to maintain the sovereignty, security, and integrity of the country during times of crisis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Government of India Act 1935** was the last pre-independence constitution of India, and it served as the basis for the Constitution of India adopted in 1950.
 
• It introduced provincial autonomy, which allowed Indian provinces to govern themselves to a certain extent, reducing the powers of the British Governor-General.
 
• The Act also provided for the establishment of a Federal Court and outlined a federal structure for India, which influenced the federal nature of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Many principles and administrative structures established by the 1935 Act were retained and refined in the Indian Constitution, contributing to the stability and continuity of governance post-independence.
 
• Emergency provisions were necessary to tackle unforeseen situations that could threaten the nation, thereby providing a constitutional mechanism to handle crises effectively.

questions.question: The concept of Concurrent List in the Indian Constitution is borrowed from the Constitution of __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Australia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The concept of the **Concurrent List** in the Indian Constitution is borrowed from the **Australian Constitution**.
 
• In the **Australian federal system**, powers are divided between the federal and state governments, with concurrent powers allowing both levels of government to legislate on certain subjects.
 
• The Indian Constitution adopts this idea to allocate legislative powers between the Union and State legislatures under **Article 246** and the **Seventh Schedule**.
 
• The Concurrent List in India contains subjects on which both the Parliament and State Legislatures can legislate, but in case of a conflict, the Union law prevails (as per **Article 254**).
 
• Examples of subjects in the Concurrent List include education, forest, trade unions, and marriage laws.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution**:

 
 
• The Seventh Schedule divides legislative powers between the Union and State governments into three lists: **Union List, State List, and Concurrent List**.
 
• The Union List contains 100 subjects, the State List has 61 subjects, and the Concurrent List has 52 subjects as of the latest amendment.
 
 
 
• **Article 246**:
 
 
• It lays down the distribution of legislative powers between the Union and the States.
 
• Parliament has exclusive power to make laws on subjects in the Union List, while State Legislatures have exclusive power on the State List.
 
 
 
• **Article 254**:
 
 
• In case of a conflict between Union and State laws on a Concurrent List subject, the law made by the Union Parliament will prevail.
 
• However, a state law can prevail if it has received the President's assent.
 
 
 
• **Federal Features of the Indian Constitution**:
 
 
• Indian federalism is unique, combining the division of powers with a strong unitary bias.
 
• Features like a strong central government, single citizenship, and a unified judiciary distinguish it from purely federal systems like the USA.

• This principle divides the government into three branches: the legislature, executive, and judiciary.
 
• Each branch functions independently to prevent concentration of power and ensure a system of checks and balances.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Review in India:**
 
 
• Judicial review empowers courts to examine the constitutionality of legislative and executive actions.

• **The Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949**.

• The Constitution of India is the **longest written** constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• The **Seventh Schedule** of the Constitution contains three lists which delineate the subjects under the **Union, State, and Concurrent lists**.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in **Article 368**.
 
• The Union List has been amended several times to meet the evolving needs of the nation.
 
• While the Constitution was adopted on 26th November 1949, it **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.

• Subjects under the **Union List include defense, foreign affairs, railways, banking, among others,** where the central government has exclusive powers to legislate.
 
• The list reflects the subjects that are of national importance and require uniformity of legislation across the country.

questions.question: The Preamble to the Constitution of India is based on the Objective Resolution moved by Jawaharlal Nehru in the Constituent Assembly on ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**13 December 1946.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Preamble to the Constitution of India is based on the Objective Resolution moved by Jawaharlal Nehru in the Constituent Assembly on **13 December 1946.**

 
• The preamble was accepted by the Constituent Assembly on January 22, 1947.
 
• The Preamble to the Indian Constitution lays out the Constitution's ideas and identifies the sources of its power.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Constituent Assembly passed it on November 26, 1949, and it went into effect on **January 26, 1950, India's Republic Day.**
 
• The 42nd Amendment changed the description of India from a "sovereign democratic republic" to a "sovereign, socialist secular democratic republic", and also changed the words "unity of the nation" to "unity and integrity of the nation". 
 
• 42nd Amendment Act, 1976: After the judgment of the Kesavanand Bharati case, it was accepted that the preamble is part of the Constitution. As a part of the Constitution, the preamble can be amended under Article 368 of the Constitution, but the basic structure of the preamble cannot be amended. Hence the preamble is considered by the constitution as the basic structure of the constitution.
 
• By itself, the Preamble is not enforceable in a court of law.
 
• The Supreme Court has held that the Preamble can be considered as an aid to the legal interpretation of the Constitution, where the language is ambiguous.

__
 
• Unitary features of the constitution include -

 
 
• A strong centre
 
• The right of parliament to amend major portions of the constitution
 
• Unequal representation in Rajya Sabha
 
• A single constitution
 
• Single citizenship
 
• The flexibility of the Constitution
 
• Integrated judiciary
 
• The appointment of state governor by the centre
 
• All India services
 
• Emergency provisions
 
• Single election machinery for state/centre government elections.

questions.question: The Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly was consisted of ______ members.

• **Later, **B. L. Mitter was replaced by N. Madhava Rau, and D. P. Khaitan was replaced by T. T. Krishnamachari.

• On** 29 August 1947**, the Constituent Assembly set up a **Drafting Committee under the Chairmanship of Dr B.R. Ambedkar **to prepare a Draft Constitution for India.
 
• While deliberating upon the draft Constitution, the Assembly moved, discussed and disposed of as many as 2,473 amendments out of a total of 7,635 tabled.
 
• The Constitution of India was adopted on** 26 November 1949 **and the hon'ble members appended their signatures to it on **24 January 1950**.
